items.text: In outpatient care for adults with depression, which strategies (electronic prompts, clinician training, audit and feedback, champions, or combinations) increase the proportion of visits with a completed and clinician-reviewed symptom measure, compared with usual practice, and do the increases last after support ends?
items.population: Adults treated for depression in outpatient mental health or psychiatry services
items.intervention: Strategies to increase routine symptom measurement
items.outcome: Completed and clinician-reviewed measure per visit; persistence after support ends
items.time: End of support and latest follow-up
items.setting: Outpatient and community mental health services

items.text: In the same studies, is higher measure use associated with response or remission at six months?
items.outcome: Response or remission at about six months

finer: Feasible for two reviewers with librarian support if the second reviewer is released; interesting to the executive; novel in its harmonised definition; ethical as a review of published work; relevant to a pending purchase.
summary: Two PICO review questions: uptake with durability, and patient outcomes.
